items.title: Bound tmux option probes to one second
items.body:
Bound tmux option probes to one second

## Why

A hung tmux command or a descendant holding stdout open can block terminal input setup indefinitely.

## What changed

Run tmux option probes on a worker thread with a shared one-second deadline, returning default input options when the wait times out. Prevent overlapping probes and kill and reap commands that exceed the deadline.

Capture stdout in a temporary file so completed commands do not wait for descendants to close it, and read at most 4 KiB of output.

## Testing

Add Unix regression tests for successful output, killing and reaping a timed-out command, and returning promptly when a descendant keeps stdout open.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Current installed desktop app: 26.928.40906, build 12694 (verified 2 October 2026). The reported denial occurred on 25 September 2026; the exact app/browser-plugin build at that event is not established here. No fresh reproduction has been attempted on the current build.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this narrowly scoped report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS desktop workflow, using Browser Use through cua_repl.js. Exact historical OS and browser-plugin versions are not established in this report.

### What issue are you seeing?

Please clarify the scope of a historical browser URL-policy denial and provide a supported path for ordinary rendered TradingView chart-panel screenshots, if permitted. This report does not establish a precise platform defect or claim that the denied action is reproducible on the latest build.

On 25 September 2026 at 02:58:16.355 UTC, a Browser Use action titled "Open second-layout daily image" failed after TradingView's Take snapshot > Open in new tab flow. The failed action attempted to access the resulting generated-snapshot tab. It was not an ordinary screenshot of the rendered chart panel. Six earlier exports had worked.

Exact error:

Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy. Reason: The browser URL policy blocks this action. Browser use cannot visit the requested page because its URL is blocked by the Browser use URL policy. The agent must not attempt to achieve the same outcome via workaround, indirect execution, raw CDP or browser commands, alternate browser surfaces, or policy circumvention. Proceed only with a materially safer alternative that does not require this blocked browser action; if none exists, stop and request user input.

The error did not identify the blocked URL or exact rule. Its prohibition on alternate routes leaves unclear whether a separately supported, ordinary rendered-page screenshot would be outside the denied action. The workflow is paused pending clarification.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Historical observed sequence, not a fresh or deterministic reproducer:

1. Work in an existing authorized TradingView chart layout through Browser Use.
2. Choose TradingView's Take snapshot > Open in new tab.
3. Attempt to select/access the resulting generated-snapshot tab.
4. Receive the URL-policy rejection above and stop the blocked workflow.

No recent live retry, chart capture, permission change, or alternate retrieval was performed while preparing this report. No claim is made about whether the generated URL, its protocol, a destination rule, or another policy gate caused the denial.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please confirm whether the following ordinary UI workflow is independently permitted without opening or retrieving any generated snapshot image:

1. Open the existing authorized TradingView layout.
2. Select and temporarily expand an existing chart panel within the page, without desktop fullscreen.
3. Verify the panel identity and that its indicators have finished rendering.
4. Use the supported browser screenshot capability to capture rendered pixels.
5. Restore the original panel, layout, and sidebar state.

If permitted, please identify the documented screenshot API and required site-permission scope. If prohibited, please identify the precise policy boundary and official review or recovery path. Current browser-tool documentation describes ordinary visible-page JPEG screenshots, but that alone does not resolve the historical denial's "same outcome" restriction.

The first permitted test would be one panel only, checking restoration, readability, indicator coverage, and panel identity. Any actual JPEG screenshot would be labelled as such, rather than as a PNG export. No indirect image retrieval, raw CDP, shell route, alternate browser surface, policy bypass, or broad permission change is requested.

### Additional information

Related: #44881 concerns similar denial-scope and supported-recovery ambiguity for local previews. This report adds the distinct TradingView generated-snapshot versus rendered-panel-screenshot question; it is not an established duplicate. The repository's open-and-closed issue search for TradingView did not reveal a matching report.

Official references:
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/browser (browser workflows and site-permission controls)
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/troubleshooting (reporting guidance)

No trade details, account details, layout IDs, generated snapshot URLs, credentials, private paths, session contents, or raw logs are included. No capture or permission change was performed to prepare this report.

items.title: Use the shared text editor for command-center task renaming
items.body:
Use the shared text editor for command-center task renaming

## What changed

Replace the rename field with a single-line `TextArea` that honors configured editor bindings and the composer's Vim setting. Start renaming in insert mode and support Vim Escape recovery on legacy terminals.

Strip carriage returns and newlines from titles and pasted text, keep Vim linewise pastes inline, and scroll horizontally at grapheme boundaries to keep the cursor visible.

## Testing

Add single-line editor coverage for newline filtering, Vim commands, repeat edits, and inline yanks. Extend command-center tests to cover Vim renaming across status-filter changes and cursor placement in narrow layouts.

items.title: Support Ctrl+Insert for copying TUI selections
items.body:
Support Ctrl+Insert for copying TUI selections

## Why

Windows Terminal forwards `Ctrl+Insert` when its Copy action has no native terminal selection. Recognize this shortcut so it can copy text selected within Codex.

## What changed

Add `Ctrl+Insert` to the shared copy-key detection used by transcript and composer selections. Use the same detection for transcript input ownership so the selection consumes the shortcut before other input handlers.

## Testing

Extend transcript tests to verify `Ctrl+Insert` input ownership and copying. Extend composer tests and snapshots to verify that failed or unconfirmed copies preserve the selection, while confirmed copies clear it without changing the draft or cursor.

Markdown rich preview is available when reviewing local changes,

options menu only shows Word wrap, Word diffs and Hide imports,
with no Rich preview option.

view, matching the experience available for local changes.

the file is missing, renamed or different in the local checkout.

PRs often contain specifications, design documents and implementation
plans. Reading them as formatted Markdown would make reviews easier
without leaving Codex.

items.title: Release stable Markdown tables into scrollback during streaming
items.body:
Release stable Markdown tables into scrollback during streaming

## Why

Table holdback kept completed tables and subsequent content mutable until the response finished. Releasing completed tables earlier also requires a final scrollback reflow when late reference-link definitions change previously emitted content.

## What changed

- Release table holdback once the containing top-level Markdown block is stable, rescanning the remaining tail for later tables.
- Track completed-block boundaries across incremental and full renders.
- Request scrollback reflow at answer completion when reference-link definitions are present, including definitions pending without a trailing newline.

## Testing

Add regression assertions and snapshots for completed tables entering scrollback while later tables remain mutable, and for late reference-link definitions resolving correctly at completion. Cover reflow requests with and without a trailing newline and reference handling with inline visualizations enabled.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.928.31416 (MSIX OpenAI.Codex 26.928.3736.0, app-server 0.159.2). The same code is in 26.928.40906 and 26.930.21537 (MSIX 26.930.2377.0).

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro (5x)

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

With the app-server queue (`thread/queue/*`), stopping a turn pauses the queued follow-ups: every item shows that the queue was paused because the turn was interrupted (Japanese UI: 「中断したため、キューを一時停止しました」). Clicking **Resume** then does nothing. No `thread/queue/start` request reaches the app-server (checked in the desktop log). "Send now" and delete on a single item still work.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. In a local thread, start a turn.
2. While it runs, send one or two follow-ups so they go into the queue.
3. Stop the turn.
4. Click **Resume** on the paused queue.

Result: nothing is sent, and the queue stays paused.

### What is the expected behavior?

Resume starts the next queued item (`thread/queue/start`).

### Additional information

In the renderer bundle, the server queue's resume starts with:

```js
resume: async (threadId, isCurrent) => {
  if (manager.isConversationStreaming(threadId)) return;
  ...
  await manager.sendRequest(`thread/queue/start`, { threadId, queuedSubmissionId: item.id });
```

`isConversationStreaming(threadId)` is `streamRoles.has(threadId)`. In 26.930 it goes through `streamState.isConversationStreaming`, which is still `streamRoles.has`. That is true whenever the thread is **open in this window** (it holds a stream role), not only while a turn runs. Resume can only be clicked with the thread open, so it always returns at the first line.

Confirmed workaround: when no turn is active or starting for the thread (`submissionHost.getActiveTurnId(threadId) == null && !submissionHost.hasPendingTurnStart(threadId)`), making that one check answer `false` for the duration of the synchronous call lets Resume proceed normally. One `thread/queue/start` is sent, and a double click still sends only once.

Checking "a turn is active or starting" in that guard, instead of "the thread has a stream role", would fix it.

items.title: [Windows] One missing chunked-message acknowledgement blocks every later host→renderer message (no timeout): sends spin forever, finished turns stay on "Thinking"

labels.name: bug

labels.name: app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Seen on 26.928.40906 (MSIX OpenAI.Codex 26.928.4866.0, app-server 0.159.2). The code path described below is unchanged in 26.930.21537 (MSIX 26.930.2377.0, app-server 0.159.0-alpha.12.1).

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro (5x)

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

The primary window stops receiving every message from the host. Nothing reaches it: no replies, no notifications, no turn progress. The app-server and the main process keep working the whole time:

- A message sent from the composer spins forever. The send first waits for `thread/queue/list`, and that reply never arrives, so `turn/start` is never sent. Clicking Send again does the same.
- A turn that is running, or has already finished on the server, stays on "Thinking" in the window. The rollout file shows the turn completing (`task_complete`) several minutes later.
- Follow-ups typed while that turn is running are neither queued nor sent.
- There is no error in the UI. The desktop log keeps logging `response_routed ... targetDestroyed=false` for every request the window makes.

The state does not recover by itself. Reloading the window fixes it (in one case it took two reloads).

Measurements from one occurrence (26.928.40906, right after a cold start):

- Replies stopped reaching the window within the first minute after launch and did not resume. In the first 4.5 minutes after launch the desktop log recorded 266 `response_routed ... targetDestroyed=false` lines for this window.
- For 12 s, a `message` listener in the window recorded **zero** events.
- I sent a harmless read (`thread/loaded/list`) through `electronBridge.sendMessageFromView`. The desktop log shows it routed (`response_routed ... requestId=probe-… targetDestroyed=false`), but the window never received the reply.
- After a reload, a listener installed at document start showed a chunked transfer (`codex-host-chunked-message-v1`, start + 13 chunks + end) arriving in 2.5 s. All the queued messages (`mcp-response`, `mcp-notification`, `shared-object-updated`, …) arrived immediately after its `end`, and the window worked normally again.

### Likely cause (from the shipped main bundle)

The chunked sender in the main process (the class with `send`, `sendCritical`, `acknowledge`, `drain`, `sendNextPart`):

- Messages larger than `inlineThresholdBytes` (4 MiB) are sent as parts of 2 MiB batches.
- The next part is sent only from `acknowledge(target, transferId, sequence)`. That happens when the renderer calls `electronBridge.acknowledgeChunkedMessage(transferId, sequence)` after its window `message` handler processed the part.
- While `target.transfer != null`, `drain()` returns early. Every other message for that webContents, including small ones, is pushed to `target.messages` and waits behind the transfer.
- There is no timer on the acknowledgement. `retryDelayMs` only applies when `deliver` throws.

So if a single acknowledgement never reaches the main process, that window receives nothing until it reloads. A reload resets the transfer (`handleLoading` re-queues it, `handleLoaded` drains again), which matches what we see.

In the occurrence above I could not see which part went unacknowledged: the window started losing messages before I could record its message events. Everything else fits: the host routes, the window receives nothing, a reload starts with a large chunked transfer, and then everything flows. Right after startup is also when a message can arrive before the renderer's handlers exist. The same window also misses the one-time `codex-app-server-initialized` message at startup (#49718).

I checked one thing against the running app: an acknowledgement for a transferId/sequence the host is not waiting for is ignored, and the window keeps working. So re-acknowledging the last part the window saw is a safe client-side workaround.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Intermittent, mostly right after a cold start, with large threads open (rollouts of tens of MB with images make the large initial messages likely):

1. Start the Codex app with a few large local threads.
2. Open a large thread and send a message, or wait for a running turn.
3. Sometimes the composer spins and the thread shows no progress. The desktop log keeps logging `response_routed` for that window, and the window receives no `message` events.
4. Reload the window: everything resumes.

### What is the expected behavior?

A lost or late acknowledgement should not stop all later messages to the window. For example:

- Put a time limit on the acknowledgement, then re-send the current part or restart the transfer.
- Don't hold small messages behind an incomplete chunked transfer.
- Have the renderer report "I have no transfer in progress" on mount, so the host can restart a transfer the renderer never saw.

Requests from the renderer should also not wait without a time limit (`timeoutMs` 0). At least the composer should surface an error instead of spinning.

### Additional information

Possibly the same root cause as #45371 ("app-server responses lost during the ~20 s renderer mount; composer spins forever") and #47795 ("early `vscode://codex/*` fetch responses are silently lost at startup"). Both describe replies the host produced that never reach the window, with no error.

I wrote a local workaround that re-acknowledges a stalled part and reloads the window when routed replies stop arriving: https://github.com/tomhda/codex-app-recovery (it does not modify the app). It has only been verified on my own machine, on the versions listed above. It works around the symptom; it is not a fix.

items.body:
## Summary

While working on my Ruby/Rails codebase in the Codex app, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol frequently edited files through Python or shell scripts. The files changed on disk, but Codex's diff review displayed only a small subset of the changes.

I am reporting from a separate session because the affected sessions contain private code. The reporting session does not reproduce the issue; this report is based on my observations in the affected sessions.

## Observed behavior and impact

For example, after a task involving roughly 100 changes, only two changes were visible for review. These counts are approximate and are not a count of changed files. The incomplete diff prevents me from reviewing the agent's complete work.

items.body: ## Component - Product: Codex IDE extension for Visual Studio Code - OS: Windows - Extension version: `26.930.21537` ## Summary The Codex VS Code extension intermittently drops submitted prompts. After several successful turns, a submitted prompt disappeared from the composer and was never displayed in the chat. Inspection of the affected local session transcript confirmed that the prompt was never written to the transcript, indicating that it was lost before reaching the Codex app-server. The extension log repeatedly records `cloudflare_challenge` responses and failures to release the queued message send lock. The in-product `/feedback` command is also unavailable because its permission check fails. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the Codex extension in VS Code on Windows. 2. Run `/logout`. 3. Sign in again. 4. Start a new chat. 5. Send the following short prompts: - `こんにちは` - `テスト送信中です` - `ほんとですか？` 6. Confirm that those prompts are sent successfully. 7. Send another prompt: - `また途中で送信できなくなりませんか？` ## Actual result - The last submitted prompt disappears. - No user-message bubble is created in the chat. - No assistant response is started. - The prompt is absent from the affected local session transcript. - The prompt therefore appears to have been dropped in the IDE extension/WebView message queue before reaching the Codex app-server. The behavior is intermittent: several messages can succeed before a later message is dropped. ## Expected result - The submitted prompt should remain visible in the chat. - A new turn should be created and sent to the Codex app-server. - A failed submission should display an error without discarding the prompt text. ## Relevant extension log errors The extension log contains repeated occurrences of the following error: ```text Failed to release queued message send lock errorMessage="\"undefined\" is not valid JSON" errorName=SyntaxError ``` The stack trace points to the extension WebView code calling `JSON.parse` from `onFetchResponse`. The extension also repeatedly receives HTTP 403 responses such as: ```text errorCode=cloudflare_challenge status=403 routePattern=/accounts/optimized/check ``` and: ```text errorCode=cloudflare_challenge status=403 routePattern=/subscriptions ``` These requests originate from the VS Code extension WebView. The same queued-message lock error was also observed in logs from earlier extension versions: - `26.928.31416` - `26.928.40906` ## `/feedback` also fails Running `/feedback` displays the following notification: ```text フィードバックの送信権限を確認できませんでした。もう一度お試しください ``` English translation: ```text Could not verify permission to send feedback. Please try again. ``` The feedback form does not open, and no feedback is submitted. Feedback is not disabled in the local Codex configuration. There is no local configuration entry equivalent to: ```toml [feedback] enabled = false ``` Around the same period, the extension continued to record HTTP 403 responses with: ```text errorCode=cloudflare_challenge routePattern=/subscriptions ``` Therefore, the in-product feedback channel cannot be used to report this issue. ## Troubleshooting already attempted The following actions did not resolve the problem: - VS Code: Reload Window - Completely restarting VS Code - Restarting Windows - Running `/logout` and signing in again - Starting a new chat - Allowing the extension to update to `26.930.21537` ## Additional observations - `https://chatgpt.com` opens normally in a regular web browser. - The browser does not display a Cloudflare challenge. - The Cloudflare-related failures are observed in the VS Code extension WebView requests. - The issue is not specific to the contents of the dropped prompt. - The issue occurs before the dropped prompt is recorded in the local session transcript. - Raw logs are not attached publicly because they may contain account or session identifiers. Sanitized excerpts can be provided if needed. ## Request Please investigate: 1. Why the VS Code extension WebView receives `403 / cloudflare_challenge` for account and subscription endpoints while the same account can access `chatgpt.com` normally in a browser. 2. Why a failed WebView response results in `"undefined" is not valid JSON`. 3. Why the queued message send lock cannot be released. 4. Why the prompt text is silently discarded instead of being retained or showing a submission error. 5. Why `/feedback` cannot verify the permission to submit feedback under the same conditions. ## Screenshot A of the `/feedback` permission-check failure is attached.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.928.3736.0 (Microsoft Store package version recorded during the incident)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro (personal account)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.6466, x64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

On Windows 10 with a VPN enabled, changing an Edge DNS preference was followed by ordinary ChatGPT desktop Chat failing, while ChatGPT Work remained usable. After reopening the desktop app, ordinary Chat was no longer offered and the UI showed only **ChatGPT Work** and **Codex**. Reverting the Edge preference and restarting **Edge only** was followed by desktop Chat recovering without restarting the desktop app.

The issue is currently mitigated: using Google DNS over HTTPS in Edge allows both websites and ordinary desktop Chat to work. I am reporting the unexpected desktop behavior and the observed rollback correlation, **not claiming that the desktop app reads Edge preferences or that direct causation has been established**.

## Environment

- Incident: October 1–2, 2026, UTC+08:00.
- Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.6466.
- Desktop app: Microsoft Store package `OpenAI.Codex`, version `26.928.3736.0` recorded during the incident; UI includes ChatGPT Chat, Work and Codex.
- Microsoft Edge: `154.0.4258.48`, recorded in its NetLog.
- Personal Pro account; ordinary conversations remained accessible on the web during the desktop failure.
- Configured DNS resolver: local router `192.168.31.1`. Windows system proxy was disabled; WinHTTP was direct.
- Other VPN/network-filter software was present, so this was not a clean networking environment.
- The desktop app had been manually updated through the Microsoft Store earlier that day after previous automatic update failures. This is a possible confounding factor, not an identified cause.

## Observed sequence

This is one observed change-and-rollback sequence, not a reliably repeatable reproduction procedure.

| Stage | Edge / websites | Ordinary desktop Chat | Work |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial state, VPN Smart mode | Google, ChatGPT and other sites timed out | Working | Working |
| Add Edge preference below and restart Edge | Tested websites worked | Subsequently failed | Remained usable |
| Reopen desktop app; also try signing out and back in | Web conversations remained available | Only Work/Codex available; ordinary Chat/history absent from desktop UI | Usable |
| Remove added Edge preference and restart Edge only | Website failures returned | Chat entry and history returned; user confirmed recovery | Usable |
| Later enable Google DoH through Edge settings | User confirmed external websites working | User confirmed ordinary Chat working | Usable |

The initial workaround added this top-level value to **Edge's** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Local State`:

```json
"async_dns": {
  "enabled": false
}
```

The entire `async_dns` property had previously been absent. No corresponding preference was written to the desktop app. Windows DNS servers, hosts, VPN mode/node and desktop login data were not changed as part of that preference edit. An earlier Windows DNS cache flush was another troubleshooting action.

Desktop symptoms included `Unknown error` when sending a new message, a disabled send button in existing conversations despite entered text, and failure to synchronize newly created web conversations. After reopening, the desktop label changed to **ChatGPT Work**, and ordinary Chat disappeared. Signing out and back in did not restore it. Desktop logs contained `net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`, but no desktop network capture established its DNS destination or a causal connection to the Edge preference.

At **2026-10-01 22:43 UTC+08:00**, the rollback removed only the added Edge preference. The rollback record confirms `AsyncDnsAbsent: true`, `OtherPreferencesUnchanged: true`, and `ChatGPTStopped: false`. Edge was restarted; the desktop process was left running. The user then confirmed desktop Chat had recovered. Cloud conversation history was never observed to be lost.

## Network evidence and its limits

An **Edge NetLog captured after rollback**, when desktop Chat worked but the ChatGPT website failed, showed:

```text
Host: chatgpt.com
DNS transaction: DNS_TRANSACTION_TCP_ATTEMPT
DNS server: 192.168.31.1:53
Extracted A record: 199.59.149.230
TCP destination: 199.59.149.230:443
Result after approximately 21 seconds: os_error=10060, net_error=-118
Error: ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT
```

This is a sanitized summary, not a verbatim log excerpt. The request failed before completing TCP/TLS/HTTP authentication. The browser proxy result was `DIRECT`, which does not exclude transparent VPN interception.

Three independent default `Resolve-DnsName` queries to the same resolver returned `104.18.32.47` and `172.64.155.209`. Forced-TCP queries returned `108.160.165.147` once and `128.242.240.125` twice. A request pinned to `199.59.149.230` timed out before TLS; a request pinned to `104.18.32.47` completed TLS and received HTTP 200, although the full response did not finish within the test's six-second deadline.

These observations identify an abnormal DNS response path for the **browser failure**. They do **not** establish that the desktop failure used that same path, or whether the VPN, router, upstream resolver or intervening network produced the abnormal responses.

Separately, switching the VPN to Global mode made both browser and desktop access fail; returning to Smart mode restored desktop access. Google also became reachable before some other websites without a new settings change. Network state therefore varied during troubleshooting.

## Working configuration

Through Edge's normal settings UI, I enabled **Use secure DNS** and selected the custom provider `https://dns.google/dns-query`. Read-only inspection confirmed:

```json
"dns_over_https": {
  "mode": "secure",
  "templates": "https://dns.google/dns-query{?dns}"
}
```

`async_dns` remains absent. This final step did not change the desktop app configuration, Windows DNS servers, hosts or VPN mode, and did not restart the apps. The user verified both web access and ordinary desktop Chat. This is a workaround verified in this environment, not a proposed universal fix.

## Expected behavior and questions

I expected ordinary Chat to remain identifiable during a connection failure, with an actionable error/retry state, rather than its entry and history disappearing from the desktop UI while Work still functioned.

1. Can failed Chat authentication or capability initialization cause this Work-only UI state? Which diagnostics would distinguish that from account entitlement or feature configuration?
2. Do ordinary Chat and Work use different network sessions or initialization paths that could explain partial failure in this environment?
3. What sanitized diagnostics would help investigate the Edge-change/desktop-recovery correlation?

The Edge rollback also restarted Edge, and the environment included VPN/filter software, changing network conditions and an earlier desktop update. Shared networking state, timing or reconnects remain possible explanations. No clean-environment reproduction, repeated controlled trial, or proof of shared Edge/desktop preferences is available.

## Related reports

- [#46945 — Windows report of missing ordinary Chat](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/46945)
- [#48700 — Report of missing Chat/Work toggle](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48700)

These reports describe similar UI symptoms; I have not established that they have the same cause. Raw network logs and account screenshots are not attached to this report.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is the observed sequence from one incident, not a confirmed reliable reproduction procedure.

1. On Windows 10 with the VPN in Smart mode, ordinary desktop ChatGPT Chat and Work worked, but several websites in Edge timed out.
2. With Edge closed, add "async_dns": {"enabled": false} to Edge's Local State file, then reopen Edge.
3. Websites became accessible, but ordinary desktop Chat subsequently failed to send messages or synchronize conversations. Work remained usable.
4. After reopening the desktop app, ordinary Chat and its history disappeared from the desktop UI, leaving Work/Codex available. Signing out and back in did not help.
5. Remove the added async_dns property and restart Edge only, leaving the desktop app running.
6. Ordinary desktop Chat and its history returned, while website failures returned.

The rollback also restarted Edge. VPN/network state and timing are possible confounding factors; direct causation has not been established.

### What is the expected behavior?

Ordinary Chat should remain identifiable during a connection failure, with an actionable error and retry option.

A temporary network or initialization failure should not make the ordinary Chat entry and conversation history disappear from the desktop UI while Work remains usable.

If Chat is unavailable because of a failed authentication or capability request, the app should explain that state rather than appearing to have lost access to ordinary conversations.

### Additional information

The issue is currently mitigated. After restoring the original absence of the async_dns property, enabling Secure DNS in Edge with https://dns.google/dns-query allowed both websites and ordinary desktop Chat to work.

No desktop app DNS preference, Windows DNS server setting, or hosts entry was changed for this final workaround.

The detailed timeline, sanitized Edge NetLog findings, and limitations are included in the issue description above. The Edge capture explains a browser connection failure, but does not establish the cause of the earlier desktop Chat failure.

Cloud conversation history remained intact throughout the incident.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant to local sandbox child initialization; no model request occurs.

### Which model were you using?

None; failure occurs before a model request.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows Server 2025 Standard, x64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Windows Service in Session 0; no interactive terminal.

### Codex doctor report

```json
Not collected in this bounded service-context reproduction.
```

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex CLI 0.160.0 runs in Session 0 under a non-administrator Windows virtual service account on Windows Server 2025 Standard. The unelevated sandbox initializes. Absolute-path cmd.exe and hostname.exe execute, but absolute-path Windows PowerShell, a packaged node.exe, and whoami.exe exit 0xC0000142 without expected output. Each executable succeeds when launched directly under the same service identity outside Codex. Windows process-start tracing confirms Codex created the failing children under the service user SID; the failure follows process creation. We have not identified a failing module, token restriction, or subsystem. The status code alone does not establish one. This blocks use of the CLI in the service context.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Run Codex CLI 0.160.0 as a non-administrator Windows virtual service account in Session 0 on Windows Server 2025 Standard, with a service-owned Codex home and an approved disposable workspace. Configure the Windows unelevated sandbox.
2. Confirm sandbox startup with `codex sandbox -P :workspace --include-managed-config -C <approved-workspace> <absolute-path-to-cmd.exe> /d /c echo READY`. An approved workspace write succeeds; writes to `.git` and outside the workspace are denied.
3. From that same service context, compare direct child launches with launches through the Codex unelevated sandbox, using absolute executable paths:

| Executable | Direct | Codex unelevated sandbox |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cmd.exe | exit 0, output | exit 0, output |
| hostname.exe | exit 0, output | exit 0, output |
| powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command <marker> | exit 0, output | 0xC0000142, no output |
| packaged node.exe --version | exit 0, output | 0xC0000142, no output |
| whoami.exe /user | exit 0, output | 0xC0000142, no output |

Process-start tracing confirms creation of each failing child by Codex under the service user SID. The failing children exited too quickly to establish their complete restricted groups, integrity level, or privileges. The system directory, service profile, temporary directories, Codex home, and approved workspace were accessible in direct and sandbox checks. PATH changes were observed, but the failing launches used absolute paths. Bounded Application, Code Integrity, and Security log checks did not identify a failing module; WER and SideBySide Operational channels were unavailable. MinGit was not tested.

### What is the expected behavior?

If this service-host configuration is supported, ordinary supported Windows child tools should initialize in the unelevated sandbox, or Codex should provide a diagnostic explaining why they cannot. The solution should not require making the parent service Administrator or LocalSystem.

### Additional information

Questions for maintainers:
1. Is the unelevated Windows sandbox supported when Codex runs in Session 0 as a Windows virtual service account?
2. If supported, what restricted-token, integrity, profile, desktop/window-station, environment, or host-policy prerequisites apply to these child tools?
3. What additional bounded diagnostics would identify why creation succeeds but initialization exits 0xC0000142 for selected tools?

Related: #46412 reports a similar Session 0 executable split in a different environment and proposes a desktop/USER32 mechanism. Our evidence has not established that mechanism or a common root cause. #50163 is a separate Elevated sandbox setup-mutex failure under the same identity type; the unelevated sandbox here starts successfully.

We did not make the service Administrator, switch to LocalSystem or an interactive developer, disable sandboxing, patch Codex or DLLs, change global DLL search policy, disable security controls, broaden filesystem ACLs, or bypass permission hooks. Sanitized additional diagnostics can be supplied on request.

## What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.160.0`, the npm latest release at the time of this check.

## Authentication

ChatGPT authentication. The CLI and desktop app use the same account. Token refresh succeeds. No API key is in use.

## Platform

macOS, `Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm`. I ran these checks through a terminal PTY.

## What issue are you seeing?

I can see two owned, Private environments in Settings > Codex Cloud. Neither has an Unpublished badge. The settings catalog returns both environments with current versions when requested with `scope=user&omitDraft=true`; it returns no further page. The workspace catalog returns zero environments. Legacy Codex Cloud shows “No cloud environments yet”.

On the same account, `codex cloud` shows only “All Environments (Global)” in its environment picker. I get the same result from a checkout with a GitHub remote and from `/tmp`.

An explicit submission exits 1 with:

```text
Error: no cloud environments are available for this workspace
```

The CLI's catalog requests return HTTP 200. Its repository-specific lookup returns zero environments. `codex cloud list --json` returns `{"tasks":[],"cursor":null}`; I understand that this is an execution-task list, not an environment inventory.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use a ChatGPT account with current Cloud environments visible in Settings > Codex Cloud and no environments in Legacy Codex Cloud.
2. Authenticate the latest CLI with that account.
3. Run `codex cloud`, open the environment picker, and inspect the choices without submitting.
4. Compare the picker from the repository checkout and from `/tmp`.
5. Try `codex cloud exec --env '<environment identifier>' --branch main --attempts 1 'Read-only environment canary; report pwd and git HEAD, then stop.'`.

The submission above fails during environment resolution before creating a task. No canary has run.

## What is the expected behavior?

The CLI should list accessible current Cloud environments and accept the supported identifier for fresh task dispatch. If this environment type requires a different CLI route, please document the command and identifier mapping.

The [CLI documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands#codex-cloud) describes task submission through `codex cloud exec --env`, and the [Cloud overview](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud) describes starting Cloud work from the CLI.

## Diagnostic evidence

- Current settings load `/api/codex-cloud/v1/environment-configs?scope=user&limit=100&omitDraft=true`. Its entries use `provider=caas`, stable IDs with an `asenvcfg_` component, and version IDs with a `cecfgver_` component.
- CLI 0.160.0's [environment discovery code](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/cloud-tasks/src/env_detect.rs) queries `/backend-api/wham/environments/by-repo/github/OWNER/REPO` and `/backend-api/wham/environments`.
- Its [resolve_environment_id function](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/cloud-tasks/src/lib.rs#L203) rejects an empty catalog before matching `--env`. Replacing a version ID with a stable ID therefore cannot bypass this result.
- I compared `env_detect.rs` in 0.160.0 and 0.162.0-alpha.3; the bytes match. I did not install or run the alpha release.
- `CODEX_CLOUD_TASKS_BASE_URL`, `CODEX_CLOUD_TASKS_MODE` and `CODEX_STARTING_DIFF` are unset.
- The existing doctor run passed installation/version, authentication, HTTP connectivity and the Responses WebSocket handshake. It also reported optional local MCP/state/terminal warnings; I have no evidence that they affect catalog discovery.

These observations suggest a mismatch between the current and legacy catalogs. Please confirm whether the released CLI supports the current environments and identify the supported repair or route.

Related: [#49966](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49966) reports the new/legacy selection difference in the web UI. This report supplies CLI discovery and resolution evidence. [#15544](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15544) concerns empty task-list reporting and was closed as not planned; this request concerns access to environments that exist in the current catalog.

I omitted account identifiers, environment identifiers, repository names, credentials and raw local logs.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.159.0 and 0.160.0

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant to local sandbox initialization; no model request occurs.

### Which model were you using?

None; failure occurs before any model request.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows Server 2025 Standard, build 26100, x64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Windows Service context; no interactive terminal.

### Codex doctor report

```json
Not collected in this bounded reproduction. Raw diagnostics contain private paths; sanitized excerpts are included below, and more can be supplied on request.
```

### What issue are you seeing?

Managed Elevated sandbox provisioning accepts a Windows virtual service account, exits 0, and creates a version 5 sandbox marker. Codex subsequently started under that exact non-administrator service identity cannot initialize the sandbox. In both 0.159.0 and 0.160.0, setup refresh runs; the 0.160.0 log shows:

```text
setup refresh: processed 2 write roots (read roots delegated); errors=[]
setup error: open sandbox setup mutex
```

The smoke process exits 1 before any sandboxed tool operation. This is a local sandbox initialization failure, before a model request.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows Server 2025, run a service as the virtual identity `NT SERVICE\ExenteExecutionAgent` (not Administrator or LocalSystem).
2. From an elevated provisioning process, run:

```text
codex.exe sandbox setup --elevated --user "NT SERVICE\ExenteExecutionAgent" --codex-home "<service-owned-codex-home>"
```

Setup exits 0 and creates the version 5 marker. The 0.160.0 helpers are version-matched and Authenticode-valid.
3. Under the exact target service identity, with that protected Codex home and managed workspace permissions, run:

```text
codex.exe sandbox -P :workspace --include-managed-config -C <controlled-workspace> cmd.exe /c echo CODEX_SANDBOX_READY
```

Codex starts, setup refresh reports `errors=[]`, then opening `Global\CodexSandboxSetup` fails. `CODEX_SANDBOX_READY` is not emitted. The same sequence occurs on 0.159.0 and 0.160.0.

### What is the expected behavior?

If `codex sandbox setup --elevated --user <identity>` accepts and successfully provisions an identity, Codex subsequently running under that same identity should initialize and use the Elevated sandbox without Administrator membership, or setup should clearly reject/document unsupported identity types.

### Additional information

Source observation, not a confirmed root cause: [`setup_mutex.rs` at rust-v0.160.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/setup_mutex.rs) names `Global\CodexSandboxSetup` and uses `D:P(A;;GA;;;SY)(A;;GA;;;BA)`. The file has the same Git blob SHA at the 0.159.0 and 0.160.0 tags. The mutex security descriptor appears consistent with the observed failure because it grants access to SYSTEM and Administrators while the successfully provisioned target virtual service identity belongs to neither group. Please confirm whether this explains the failure and whether it is the intended security contract.

Questions:
1. Is a Windows virtual service account such as `NT SERVICE\ExenteExecutionAgent` a supported target for `codex sandbox setup --elevated --user ...`?
2. If yes, what supported provisioning/runtime mechanism allows it to open the global mutex without Administrator membership?
3. If no, which Windows identity types are supported, and should setup reject unsupported virtual service identities?

We are keeping the service non-administrator and are not switching to LocalSystem, an interactive human account, the unelevated sandbox, or an ad hoc mutex DACL. No binary or sandbox security policy was patched. Additional sanitized diagnostics are available on request.

items.body:
Bound in-flight file opens in exec-server

## Why

The per-connection limit of 128 file read handles was checked only after opening the file, leaving pending opens outside the limit.

## What changed

Reserve a semaphore permit before polling the file-open future, counting pending opens and registered handles against the same limit. Release capacity when an open fails or is cancelled, or when a handle closes, even if a read still retains the file.

Use synchronous handle-table locks that never cross an await, and recheck duplicate IDs after opening to preserve the winning handle during concurrent opens.

## Testing

Add tests for stalled-open progress, pending-open admission limits, permit cleanup after failure or cancellation, capacity reuse while a file remains in use, and concurrent duplicate IDs.

items.body:
## Summary

From a local Codex Desktop chat, the native app tools can enumerate and read chats on a connected Remote Control Mac, but `list_projects` exposes no projects from that host. The advertised `create_thread` schema has no host selector for a projectless chat. This leaves no exposed native tool route to create a dedicated projectless chat on the connected computer, although the app's New chat → Work in → Remote flow succeeds immediately.

## Environment

- Source and destination: macOS, Apple Silicon.
- Connection: Codex Desktop Remote Control, not SSH.
- Source app: `26.928.31416`, build `12553`, bundle ID `com.openai.codex`.
- Running and installed source builds both report `12553`; running commit `69c39c76da78edf143e380efffe94e49f10da8e0`.
- Destination remote app-server: `0.159.2`; a current successful connection is recorded.

## Reproduction

1. Connect a second Mac through Remote Control.
2. From a local chat, call `list_threads` and `read_thread` with the connected host ID. Both work; the inventory reports no unavailable hosts.
3. Call `list_projects({})`. Repeated calls return source-local projects and shared ChatGPT projects, with zero destination-host projects. Its advertised contract says it lists local, remote, and ChatGPT projects.
4. Inspect `create_thread`: `target` accepts `project`, `projectless`, or `chatgptWorkCloud`. The projectless branch accepts only `directoryName`, with no destination-host field.
5. Create a projectless setup chat with a host guard. The result correctly reports `hostId: local`; the guard confirms it is on the source Mac and performs no changes.
6. Attempt `handoff_thread` for that chat with the connected destination host. It returns `Only project-scoped Git repository chats can be handed off.` This is an explicit limitation, not evidence of a failed Git handoff.
7. Use the native UI's New chat → Work in → Remote, select the connected Mac, and send the same guarded setup prompt. The resulting chat is immediately listed under the correct remote host and verifies its execution there.

## Expected

Expose a supported native tool route for creating a projectless chat on a specified connected Remote Control host, matching the existing UI capability. Alternatively, expose supported host discovery and remote project registration so an agent can establish a valid remote project target without UI control.

## Read-only implementation evidence

Inspection of the installed bundle confirms:

- `create_thread` can route through an already-discovered saved remote project ID, converting it to an internal `remoteProject` target.
- The public projectless target preserves the local default host; only the internal `remoteProject` target selects another host.
- `list_projects` explicitly fetches local projects, then consults an existing project selector. It does not explicitly fetch remote projects. Project Git metadata lookups use `Promise.allSettled` and discard rejected entries without reporting them.
- `create_project` and `list_hosts` schemas exist in the installed bundle but neither Codex capability appears in this task's live tool registry, including deferred-tool discovery.
- The source's saved remote project state contains no project associated with this particular destination. Therefore zero returned destination projects is not by itself proof of a connection failure or a remote-project listing regression.

A supported workaround is to register a destination folder as a saved remote project through the native UI, then use its discovered project ID. Direct remote projectless UI creation also works. Neither avoids UI control with the currently exposed native tools.

## Actual and workaround

Remote chat reads and UI creation work, while native project discovery and projectless host selection do not provide that route. The task required Computer Use solely to launch the remote chat. Subsequent native remote chat reads and title updates work.

No restart, reconnection, database edit, cache patch, or security change was performed. Active chats were preserved. The guarded source-local staging chat made no setup changes and was archived after the remote launch succeeded.

## Related reports

- #29284 concerns failure to match saved Git projects during cross-host handoff. This reproduction is projectless and stops at the documented Git-only handoff boundary.
- #30626 concerns SSH-side child placement. This reproduction starts on a local Mac and explicitly needs a Remote Control destination.
- #24280 concerns missing automation tools after remote creation. This report concerns the creation/discovery route itself.

The exact private host names, paths, chat IDs, prompts, and raw logs are omitted.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0, arm64

### What issue are you seeing?

An MCP App works from the global entry point and in some local tasks, but fails in certain durable (dot) conversations. Desktop logs show the same thread ID used with `hostId=DURABLE` for a successful inline call and later with `hostId=LOCAL` for a failing side-panel call. The error is `-32600: thread not found: THREAD_A` and the host eventually shows “Unable to display Reader”.

This affects both a local stdio Reader 0.1.1 and a separate remote MCP Apps diagnostic probe 0.0.3. The global/thread entry points are declared. In the remote probe, the HTML version and successful `chatgpt` host handshake were visible before the app tool call failed.

Sanitized observations, 2026-10-02 UTC (LOCAL, DURABLE and THREAD_A are placeholders):

- 02:32:34.072: `reader_probe_read`, `hostId=LOCAL`, `threadId=THREAD_A` → `-32600 thread not found` in about 1.2 ms. The remote server recorded no corresponding read request during 02:32:33–02:32:49.
- 02:37:10.548: inline read for THREAD_A with `hostId=DURABLE` succeeds. A session-removal event follows.
- 02:37:12.856: side-panel call for the same THREAD_A with `hostId=LOCAL` immediately fails.
- 02:37:27.542: a read from a separate task reaches the remote server (HTTP 200); the desktop operation completes successfully in 533.6 ms.

Affected threads also had successful resume events before failures. This is not a claim that all MCP App panels fail.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed desktop sequence (not yet a deterministic fresh-thread reproducer):

1. Install an MCP App with global and thread entry points. Reader’s public implementation is linked below.
2. Confirm the global entry works.
3. Open the app in an affected durable conversation and use its inline and side-panel surfaces.
4. Compare the desktop host/thread metadata for successful and failing app calls. In the captured sequence, the thread ID stays the same while the host changes from DURABLE to LOCAL.
5. Observe the immediate `thread not found` error and host fallback.

The exact UI action that causes the host change is still undetermined.

A separate isolated control used two instances of the bundled app-server with the same Reader configuration:
- Instance A owns THREAD_A: the call succeeds.
- Instance B receives THREAD_A: `-32600 thread not found`, before MCP dispatch.
- `config/mcpServer/reload` on B does not fix that request.
- B using its own thread succeeds with the same HTML.

This control demonstrates the wrong-instance failure mode; it does not reproduce the desktop routing trigger.

### What is the expected behavior?

Keep each MCP App session bound to the thread’s owning host/executor across resource loading, opening the panel, and app tool calls. If the owning context is unavailable, recover/resume it or show a specific recoverable error rather than sending its thread ID to a different host. The plugin should not need to repair host/thread routing.

### Additional information

- Desktop application identifies itself as ChatGPT 26.928.31416 (build 12553); bundled Codex app-server: 0.159.2.
- Public local plugin: https://github.com/Quiyyy/reader-plugin/tree/d90b911d80df6f1e0c2f4ca27f1fbc7711ee4947
- Entry-point registration: https://github.com/Quiyyy/reader-plugin/blob/d90b911d80df6f1e0c2f4ca27f1fbc7711ee4947/src/server/mcp.ts
- Passing plugin CI: https://github.com/Quiyyy/reader-plugin/actions/runs/36893521512
- Related: #34195 reports MCP resource reads before `thread/resume`. Here, successful prior resumes and different host IDs for the same thread are recorded, so I cannot establish that it is the same defect.

The host mismatch is observed in desktop logs; its internal cause is not proven, and no complete internal socket trace was captured. The remote diagnostic endpoint, real thread IDs, account information, local paths, and user content are intentionally omitted.

items.body:
### Summary

Codex panics on every shell tool call if **any** environment variable contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8. The tool call aborts, the model only sees "the tool aborted", and no command can run until the offending variable is removed from the environment.

### Environment

- codex-cli 0.160.0 (brew cask, `/opt/homebrew/bin/codex`), latest stable at the time of writing
- macOS 15.6.1, arm64
- Reproduced with `codex exec`, and in the Codex desktop app's Bash tool with the same panic
- Not caused by hooks or any third-party hook: reproduced with an isolated `CODEX_HOME` containing only `config.toml` + `auth.json` (no `hooks.json`), and with no hook configured at all

### Reproduction

1. Put a non-UTF-8 value into any environment variable. Real-world trigger: a variable exported from a legacy config file that is not valid UTF-8. Minimal synthetic version:

```python
import os, pathlib, subprocess, tempfile
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
pathlib.Path(d, "a").touch()
env = dict(os.environb)
env[b"BADVAR"] = b"\xff"  # a single invalid byte is enough
subprocess.run(
    ["codex", "exec", "--skip-git-repo-check", "-C", d, f"Run: mv {d}/a {d}/b"],
    env=env,
)
```

2. Codex starts normally, issues the shell call, and the call aborts.

### Actual result

```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' (10151524) panicked at /rustc/59807616e1fa2540724bfbac14d7976d7e4a3860/library/std/src/env.rs:162:83:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "\xFF"
stack backtrace:
   3: <std::env::Vars as core::iter::traits::iterator::Iterator>::next
   4: codex_protocol::shell_environment::create_env
   5: codex_core::exec_env::create_env
   ...
ERROR codex_core::util: in-flight tool future failed during drain:
  Fatal error: tool task failed to receive: JoinError::Panic(Id(1666), "called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: \"\\xFF\"", ...)
```

(Frame names from a `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` run; some neighbouring frames may be misattributed by inlining, but `codex_protocol::shell_environment::create_env` is consistent across runs.)

The model sees only that the command was aborted and cannot distinguish this from a permission denial. Every subsequent shell call panics identically; in my run three consecutive attempts all aborted, and the target command never executed.

### Expected

Codex should tolerate non-UTF-8 environment values. The simplest correct behaviours would be to pass them through untouched (they are legal in a POSIX environment), pass them lossily, or drop just those entries. Panicking the runtime task is never appropriate here.

### Root cause / suggested fix

`std::env::vars()` is used while assembling the environment for the child shell (`codex_protocol::shell_environment::create_env`). `env::vars()` converts each entry with `OsString::into_string().unwrap()`, so a single non-UTF-8 value panics the tokio task and the tool future fails with `JoinError::Panic`.

Switching that call site to `std::env::vars_os()` and converting with `to_string_lossy()`, or filtering out entries that fail `into_string()`, would remove the panic.

### Impact

Any user with a non-UTF-8 value in their environment, which is common with legacy locale tooling, mojibake config files, or variables inherited from an older shell, gets a completely unusable Codex for shell work. The failure message points at nothing in particular, so the actual cause is hard to find.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

When using Codex Desktop on Windows with the agent running in WSL2, the WSL terminal and project can work normally, but Codex command execution fails before even simple commands such as `pwd` or `ls` start:

```text
Failed to create unified exec process: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

### Temporary workaround

In my environment, the issue is temporarily resolved by bind-mounting Codex's Linux-side `arg0` directory to the Windows-mounted Codex `arg0` path.

Example:

```bash
sudo mount --bind \
  /home/<linux-user>/.codex/tmp/arg0 \
  /mnt/c/Users/<windows-user>/.codex/tmp/arg0
```

After that, Codex command execution works again in WSL.

You can verify the mount with:

```bash
findmnt /mnt/c/Users/<windows-user>/.codex/tmp/arg0
```

### Make the workaround survive WSL shutdown

A normal bind mount disappears after:

```powershell
wsl --shutdown
```

To recreate it automatically when WSL starts, add this to `/etc/fstab`:

```fstab
/home/<linux-user>/.codex/tmp/arg0 /mnt/c/Users/<windows-user>/.codex/tmp/arg0 none bind,nofail 0 0
```

Then restart WSL.

### Rollback

To remove the workaround:

```bash
sudo umount /mnt/c/Users/<windows-user>/.codex/tmp/arg0
```

Then remove or comment out the corresponding line in:

```text
/etc/fstab
```

### Notes

This is only a temporary workaround that fixes the issue in my environment. I am not claiming this is the root cause for every unified-exec `ENOENT` failure.

Related reports: #49731, #49904, #49969.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.928.31416 (build 12553), prod channel; bundled CLI 0.159.2

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-34-generic x86_64 unknown (Ubuntu 26.04.1, X11)

### What issue are you seeing?

Every in-app browser action fails on every origin (example.com, Wikipedia, IANA, YouTube, Google Drive/Vids) with:

> Browser Use could not complete this action because a browser security check was unavailable. Reason: The admin-enforced policy could not be verified, so access was not granted.

There is no admin policy. `configRequirements/read` returns null for `allowBrowserAndComputerUse`, `browserUse`, `inAppBrowser`, `computerUse`, `network` and `featureRequirements`, and `config.browser_use` is null.

**Root cause (reproduced):**

1. Chats inside a ChatGPT project run with cwd `~/.codex/.chatgpt-projects/g-p-<id>`, and each chat's `node_repl` MCP host inherits that cwd.
2. The project-file sync (`app.asar`, `async function DC({downloadFile,files,...})`) replaces the folder: it builds `.<name>-staging-<uuid>`, runs `rename(root, .<name>-previous-<uuid>)` and `rename(staging, root)`, then deletes the previous folder.
3. Every running `node_repl` is left with a deleted cwd: `readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd` → `.../.g-p-<id>-previous-<uuid> (deleted)`.
4. For the origin policy check, `browser-service.mjs` calls `nodeRepl.config.readRequirements()` and `nodeRepl.config.read({cwd, includeLayers:false})`. `node_repl` serves these by spawning `codex app-server` (`CODEX_CLI_PATH`), which inherits the deleted cwd and exits immediately with `Error: No such file or directory (os error 2)`.
5. `hQ()` in `browser-service.mjs` (`try{...readRequirements(),readAll()...}catch{return "unavailable"}`) maps that transport failure to `enterprise_policy_unavailable`, which surfaces as the misleading "admin-enforced policy" message.

Creating a new chat in the project triggers the swap itself, so a new chat is broken from its first browser call. Restarting the app only helps until the next swap. Rebinding the browser UI or reopening the chat does not help, because the same `node_repl` host is reused.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Linux, open a chat inside a ChatGPT project and use the in-app browser on example.com. It works.
2. Create another chat in the same project.
3. `readlink /proc/$(pgrep -x node_repl | head -1)/cwd` now ends in `.g-p-<id>-previous-<uuid> (deleted)`.
4. Use the in-app browser in either chat. Every origin fails with the error above.

Standalone confirmation:

```
cd /proc/<node_repl pid>/cwd && /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex app-server
# Error: No such file or directory (os error 2)   (exit 1)
```

From a valid directory, the same binary answers `initialize`, `configRequirements/read` and `config/read` successfully.

Observed timeline (2026-10-02, UTC+8), with a watcher sampling `node_repl` cwd every 2 s:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 09:24 | App fully quit; no Codex processes |
| 09:26–09:32 | App reopened; all `node_repl` hosts have a valid cwd |
| 09:32:25 | New chat created in the project (`thread/start`); its `node_repl` starts |
| 09:32:28 | Project folder replaced; all 4 running `node_repl` hosts switch to a deleted cwd in the same sample |
| 09:32–09:33 | In-app browser test and retry both fail with the policy error |

The same pattern occurred earlier: the browser worked at 00:45–00:46, the folder was swapped at 00:46:18, and everything failed afterwards.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Browser Use should work regardless of project-folder resyncs.
- A failure to reach the policy source should not be reported as an administrator policy.

### Additional information

**Suggested fixes:**

1. Update the ChatGPT project folder in place, or keep a stable directory, instead of renaming and deleting a directory that running hosts use as their cwd.
2. Spawn `codex app-server` from `node_repl` with an explicit existing `current_dir` (e.g. `CODEX_HOME`). Cwd-dependent config is already passed via the `cwd` parameter.
3. In `browser-service.mjs`, distinguish "policy source unreachable" from "admin policy" and surface the underlying error (e.g. "could not start codex app-server: No such file or directory").

**Platform:** Confirmed on Linux. macOS has the same POSIX deleted-cwd semantics, so it is probably affected (not tested). Windows normally refuses to rename a directory that is in use as a cwd, so it may differ.

**Possibly related** (same symptom, cause not identified there): #42466, #46295, #49301, #46350, #49270. Other reports may have different triggers, but any exception in the config bridge produces this same message.

No security settings, policies, credentials or app files were modified during diagnosis.

## Summary

Cloud tasks show inconsistent visibility and message-submission behavior across clients and creation paths. Some tasks created by dot can be read and continued through dot, but do not appear in the user's web or iOS task lists. Conversely, user-created cloud tasks can be read through dot, but attempts to continue them through dot fail.

These may be separate issues. Please clarify which task-access paths are supported; this report does not assume a shared root cause.

## Environment

- Observed October 1–2, 2026 UTC; user-reported local dates use UTC+8
- Windows ChatGPT/Codex desktop app, Microsoft Edge web, and iOS
- Exact app/browser versions were not captured
- A saved, published cloud coding environment; both user-created tasks and dot-created tasks
- The successful dot-created diagnostic task used GPT-6.1 Sol / xhigh

## Reproduction A: dot-created task executes, but is absent from web/iOS lists

1. Ask dot to create a minimal read-only task using the saved cloud configuration.
2. Wait for execution and read the result.
3. Send a second read-only instruction through dot to that same task, then read its result.
4. Check the same account's desktop, web, and iOS task lists.

**Tool-confirmed:** creation succeeded; the task executed commands against the expected repository commit and a private asset, with successful exit codes. The second instruction was accepted and executed, and its result was read successfully.

**Owner-reported:** the task appears in the desktop Codex recent-task list after an app update, but is absent from the web and iOS lists. Whether this particular task's full conversation can be opened on desktop has not yet been verified. List absence is not evidence of data loss.

Earlier create calls using an older saved configuration returned UNKNOWN / AppServerBackendRequestError. Creation later succeeded with a newly configured environment, so creation is **not currently universally broken**.

## Reproduction B: user-created task can be read, but dot cannot continue it

1. Create a cloud chat directly from desktop or mobile and send an initial message.
2. Ask dot to read that exact task.
3. Ask dot to send a minimal read-only follow-up to the same task.

**Actual:** reading succeeds, but follow-up submission returns NOT_FOUND / CloudThreadNotFoundError. The identifiers used for read and send were checked and matched. No successful submission through this send path was observed.

A null parentThreadId does not explain this observation by itself: the successfully continued dot-created diagnostic task also returned null.

## Reproduction C: browser follow-up fails, native-client follow-up works

Submitting a follow-up to an existing user-created cloud task through the dot's normal cloud-browser UI failed with:

> Error submitting message
> Unable to determine project root for task

One page refresh and retry produced the same error. Read-back confirmed that no new message or execution turn had been created; the unsent diagnostic draft was cleared.

The owner subsequently submitted a read-only check through the desktop client. It executed successfully and returned the repository commit and asset metadata; dot could read that response. The owner also reports that mobile access works.

This overlaps with #49497, but identical error text does not establish an identical cause.

Separately, the owner reports that enabling TUN in their own proxy setup resolved a Windows reconnection problem. That does not establish the cause of the cloud-browser project-root error or dot's NOT_FOUND response. No proxy/security configuration was changed by the reporting assistant.

## Impact and requested resolution

The intended workflow is one cloud coding task, with dot sending instructions and reviewing results, while the owner can inspect the same conversation across clients. Current behavior forces a choice between assistant control and consistent owner visibility.

Please:
- document supported read/continuation behavior for user-created versus dot-created tasks;
- make task discoverability consistent, or clearly explain intentional differences;
- return an actionable explanation when read succeeds but send returns NOT_FOUND;
- provide a supported task/project-association check and repair that preserves prepared environments and uncommitted work.

Archive/delete issues are tracked separately in #46182 and #46240; they are not claimed to share this root cause.

This report was prepared with the user's dot at the owner's request. It distinguishes tool/browser-confirmed execution from owner-reported client behavior. items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, a heartbeat automation targeting an existing local-project thread can replace the selected named permission profile with a generic approval mode.

My threads are configured to use the named permission profile `youtube-pi-dev`. After affected scheduled runs, the UI changes from that profile to the Japanese label `代わりに承認`.

For one affected thread, the captured execution logs also show that:

- `active_permission_profile` disappears.
- The recorded filesystem permission definition changes.
- An explicit write entry for the project directory is no longer present.
- `approval_policy` and `approvals_reviewer` remain unchanged.

A read-only investigation of the installed application's bundled JavaScript identified a likely cause: the heartbeat request-construction path receives the saved named profile but does not forward its ID. Instead, it explicitly sends the legacy `sandboxPolicy` to `turn/start`.

No proposed fix has been applied to the installed application. The original reproduction and the additional observation on October 2 occurred without applying the proposed patch.

## Environment

- Operating system: Windows 11
- Installed app package: `OpenAI.Codex`
- Desktop app version inspected: `26.928.3736.0`
- Application code collected: October 2, 2026, approximately 01:21 JST
- CLI version recorded in the affected thread's `session_meta`: `0.159.2`
- Local project directory: `D:\program_works\python\youtube_pi_agent_gui`
- Named permission profile: `youtube-pi-dev`
- Profile inheritance: `:workspace`
- Approval policy in the compared records: `on-request`
- Approvals reviewer in the compared records: `auto_review`
- Automation type: `heartbeat`, targeting an existing thread
- Schedule for the directly investigated automation: every 30 minutes

The `0.159.2` value above comes from recorded session metadata. It is not a separately verified identification of every runtime process active during the investigation.

The project configuration contains `default_permissions = "youtube-pi-dev"`, and the project is marked as trusted. The named profile is defined in the configuration and is present in normal/manual turn records.

## Expected behavior

A heartbeat automation targeting a thread should preserve the named permission profile selected for that thread, including its identity and intended permissions, subject to applicable managed restrictions.

For a thread using `youtube-pi-dev`, the scheduled request should preserve that selection through `permissions: "youtube-pi-dev"` or an equivalent supported mechanism.

It should not silently replace the named profile with a legacy sandbox-policy representation that does not retain the profile identity and may produce a different permission definition.

## Actual behavior and captured evidence

### Persisted selection

At the time of capture, the desktop's `heartbeat-thread-permissions-by-id` state still contained the named profile for the affected thread, even though intervening execution records lacked it.

The following is the captured entry with the Windows username and thread ID redacted:

```json
{
  "activePermissionProfile": {
    "id": "youtube-pi-dev",
    "extends": ":workspace"
  },
  "approvalPolicy": "on-request",
  "approvalsReviewer": "auto_review",
  "sandboxPolicy": {
    "type": "workspaceWrite",
    "writableRoots": [
      "C:\\Users\\<USER>\\.codex\\visualizations\\2026\\10\\01\\<THREAD_ID>"
    ],
    "networkAccess": true,
    "excludeTmpdirEnvVar": false,
    "excludeSlashTmp": false
  }
}
```

This shows that the named selection was present in the captured desktop state. It does not establish that every in-memory state was identical at every execution boundary.

### Execution-context comparison

The following two records come from the same affected thread on October 1, 2026. All times are JST, UTC+09:00.

| Field | 17:02:15 — named profile present | 17:16:41 — named profile absent |
|---|---|---|
| `active_permission_profile` | `{"id":"youtube-pi-dev","extends":":workspace"}` | Field absent |
| `cwd` | `D:\program_works\python\youtube_pi_agent_gui` | Same |
| `model` | `gpt-6.1-sol` | Same |
| `approval_policy` | `on-request` | Same |
| `approvals_reviewer` | `auto_review` | Same |
| Explicit project-directory write entry in the detailed filesystem policy | Present | Absent |
| Legacy `sandbox_policy.writable_roots` | Visualization directory only | Same directory |
| `exclude_tmpdir_env_var` | `false` | `true` |
| `exclude_slash_tmp` | `false` | `true` |

The legacy `writable_roots` list was the same, but the complete legacy policy was not identical because the temporary-directory flags also changed.

Representative records from that thread show the following pattern:

```text
2026-10-01 17:02:15 JST — active_permission_profile = youtube-pi-dev
2026-10-01 17:16:41 JST — active_permission_profile field absent
2026-10-01 17:17:25 JST — active_permission_profile = youtube-pi-dev
2026-10-01 17:46:41 JST — active_permission_profile field absent
2026-10-01 18:16:51 JST — active_permission_profile field absent
2026-10-01 18:21:09 JST — active_permission_profile = youtube-pi-dev
```

The recurring approximately 30-minute pattern is consistent with the automation schedule. However, not every record in this timeline has been individually correlated with a captured live request, so the timeline alone should not be treated as proof of the trigger for every entry.

### Scope of the observed impact

The logs establish a change in the recorded filesystem permission definition, not an operating-system access test.

In particular:

- The loss of the explicit project write entry was recorded.
- Actual OS-level write denial was not tested as part of this investigation.
- The disappearance of an explicit read entry for the Python installation does not prove that Python became unreadable, because a broader root-read entry remained.
- Network enablement and per-domain authorization were not treated as equivalent. Loss of all configured domain permissions has not been demonstrated.
- No sandbox escape or privilege escalation has been demonstrated.

## Reproduction pattern

This describes the pattern observed in my existing environment, not a verified clean-install minimal reproducer.

1. Use a trusted local project with a valid named permission profile.
2. Select that profile for an existing thread.
3. Confirm that a normal/manual turn records the intended `active_permission_profile`.
4. Configure a heartbeat automation targeting the same thread.
5. Let the automation run on schedule.
6. Compare the UI selection and the resulting `turn_context` with the preceding named-profile turn.

Multiple threads in the same project have exhibited the UI symptom. Detailed before/after execution-context evidence was collected for one affected thread.

The exact conditions distinguishing an affected run from a run that retains the profile are not yet established. I am not claiming that every scheduled execution fails.

## Additional observation on October 2: the previously unaffected main thread also changed

Initially, one older “main” thread appeared to retain `youtube-pi-dev`, while other threads exhibited the problem.

On the morning of October 2, 2026, JST, I also observed the permission selection change in that main thread.

At that time:

- The proposed application fix had not been applied.
- No post-fix real-device validation had been performed.

This is therefore an additional observation in an unpatched environment, not a regression caused by the proposed patch.

The main thread should no longer be described as an unaffected exception.

For this additional main-thread observation, the exact scheduled run, outgoing request, and resulting `turn_context` have not yet been correlated. I am reporting the observed selection change, not claiming that its detailed filesystem policy was separately verified.

The older main thread's captured working directory was under the previous C: location, whereas other affected threads used the D: location. This difference has not been established as the cause or a reliable workaround. The morning observation also shows that the older thread is not reliably protected from the symptom.

## Technical investigation

The installed application's `app.asar` was read without modifying the installed application.

The investigation used the complete collected JavaScript modules and traced the heartbeat request path through final JSON serialization. This was an AI-assisted analysis, with an isolated request-packaging test described below.

### 1. The heartbeat entry point drops the named selection

Function: `Jl`

The following is the complete function, formatted for readability while retaining the bundled identifiers:

    statsig: e,

    collaborationMode: i,

}) {

        }),

        prompt: u,
        collaborationMode: i,

## Suggested fix direction

Preserve the selected named profile throughout heartbeat request construction.

When a valid saved `activePermissionProfile` exists, pass its ID using `permissions` and do not simultaneously send `sandboxPolicy`.

When no named profile exists, retain the appropriate legacy behavior.
